current_evidence: The council's validation checklist page links this file as 'Adopted Validation Checklist for Planning Applications (May 2025)' and states 'An updated version has been adopted by Committee on 29th May 2025'. The document text also says it was adopted 29 May 2025, even though the URL slug still says august-2023.

issues.detail: Grokbot missed a later change on the planning page. A December 2025 note says major applications submitted after November 2025 will not be asked for the Sustainable Drainage Pro-Forma at validation until an updated version is produced.
issues.evidence: Planning page Dec 2025 note: 'for the time being this document will not be requested at validation'

issues.detail: Almost all of the 14 tab_items are process text, drawing guidance or fragments, not requirements. Examples: the 21-day invalid-application notice, the 'administrative charge will be levied' text, the pre-application service note, submission on 'CD or USB storage device', redaction instructions, 'Wherever possible the plan should be scaled to fit onto A4 or A3', and the orphan fragment 'SSSI, SPA, SAC or Ramsar sites).' Only the mineral safeguarding item is a real local requirement, and it is filed under 'Submission rules'.
The tab_items include two near-identical redaction notes ('commercially sensitive or personal information' and 'commercially sensitive information'). Neither is a requirement.

Coal Mining Risk Assessment is listed as a requirement for Householder, Listed building consent, Advertisement consent, Lawful development cert, Works to trees and Hazardous substances. The source names exactly these application types as EXEMPT from a CMRA. Grokbot treated the exemption list as a list of types that require it.
issues.evidence: 'Part A - Exempt by type of application: householder development; heritage consents...; advertisement consent; lawful development certificates; hazardous substances consent; works to trees...'

issues.detail: Three requirements are placed under Variation of condition s73 only because the source mentions s73 as an exception. The Design and Access Statement text says a DAS is NOT required for s73 applications. The Highways/access and Structural Survey excerpts cite s73 only in an 'Except where the application is made pursuant to section 73' footnote.
issues.evidence: 'Design and Access Statement are not required to accompany applications: for permission to develop land without compliance with conditions... section 73'

issues.detail: Several placements are mislabelled. The Crime Impact Statement goes under Outline, but the source applies it to 'ATMs and other developments which may increase the risk of crime' and does not mention outline. 'Street scene elevations' goes under Listed building consent, but its excerpt is the separate LBC 1:20 section-details requirement. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' goes under Full planning, but the source requires the LBC method statement for any Listed Building Consent application.
issues.evidence: 'Crime Impact Statement When required? ATM's and other developments which may increase the risk of crime'; 'Listed Building Consent When required? Applications for Listed Building Consent where elevational changes are proposed Scale? Typically 1:20'

issues.detail: About 30 requirements are 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', although the source applies them by trigger, not by application type. As a result, the only Householder entry is the coal mining item, which householders are exempt from. The source's Floor Plans, Elevations, Roof Plans, Site Levels, Sections, Streetscene, Heritage Statement, Biodiversity Report, Tree Survey/AIA and FRA triggers all catch householder and other application types.
issues.evidence: e.g. 'Floor Plans... When required? All applications which include new buildings, alterations to buildings or changes to the use of any space'

issues.detail: Many trigger excerpts are fragments or come from the wrong requirement. Flood Risk Assessment: 'a simple flood risk assessment.' (the real trigger is Flood Zones 2/3, or Zone 1 sites meeting size or flood-risk conditions). Environmental Statement: 'of the EIA Regulations...'. Foul Sewage: '...in the following order... 1.'. Transport: 'accompanied by a Transport Statement or Assessment and Travel Plan.' (no thresholds). Travel Plan: the excerpt is a Lancashire email address plus the Tree Survey text. Block/site plan: flue text plus the affordable housing trigger. Parking plan: the floor plans trigger. Photographs: land contamination text. Housing mix: affordable housing text. Advertisement drawings: lighting/ecology text. Archaeology: 'an appropriate desk-based assessment...' with no trigger.
issues.evidence: app_type_rows trigger_excerpt fields vs source 'When required?' lines

issues.detail: Two items are recorded as requirements although the source says they are not validation requirements: Planning Obligations / S106 Heads of Terms and Self-build / custom build (Unilateral Undertaking).
issues.evidence: 'Whilst planning obligations are not a validation requirement...'; 'whilst not a validation requirement, the applicant will be required to submit a Unilateral Undertaking'

issues.detail:
Several local document requirements are missing:
- AONB Major Development Test: major development in the AONB.
- Green Belt Calculations: replacement buildings and extensions in the Green Belt.
- Odour Assessment: odour-generating development near sensitive receptors, or sensitive development near odour sources such as wastewater works.
- Retail Sequential Test and Impact Assessment: main town centre uses outside centres, above the floorspace thresholds.
- Street Adoption Statement: new internal roads or connections to the public highway.
- Sustainable Drainage Pro-Forma: major development with surface water drainage, since paused.
- Telecommunications Development: all telecoms applications.
- Tree Works Application: works to TPO trees or conservation area trees. The Works to trees row lists only the exempt coal item.
- Wind Energy Applications: shadow flicker within 10x turbine height; decommissioning bond for single turbines over 40m or multiple turbines; community benefits at 250kW+; communications impacts.
- Appendix A biodiversity tables: protected species triggers in Table 1, priority habitats in Table 2, survey timings in Table 3.
issues.evidence: Section 3.0 Documents: 'AONB Major Development Test', 'Green Belt Calculations', 'Odour Assessment', 'Retail Sequential Test and Impact Assessment', 'Street Adoption Statement', 'Telecommunications Development', 'Tree Works Application', 'Wind Energy Applications'

issues.detail:
Several local plan requirements are missing:
- Site Layout Plans (existing and proposed): every application except s73/s73A.
- Site Levels Plans: new buildings, extensions, decking, engineering operations.
- Sectional Drawings: new buildings, extensions including roof lifts and basements, decking, listed building alterations, ground-level changes.
- Streetscene Plan: new buildings or height increases fronting the highway or public realm next to neighbours.
- Major housing development plans: majors where layout or appearance is considered.
- Access Ramp Details: new external ramp.
- Shopfront Details: new or altered shopfront.
issues.evidence: Section 3.0 Plans: 'Site Layout Plans', 'Sectional Drawings', 'Streetscene Plan', 'Access Ramp Details', 'Shopfront Details'

summary: Grokbot's link points to the current May 2025 checklist; only the List date is off (should be 2025-05-29). The extraction is poor: tab_items are mostly boilerplate, coal mining is assigned to exactly the application types the source exempts, DAS and other items are wrongly put under s73, many triggers are garbled, and about 10 document and 7 plan requirements are missing, including Green Belt, Odour, Retail tests, Telecoms, Tree Works and Wind Energy.

withdrawn_issues.detail: The List date is 2025-05-01, but the document and the planning page give adoption as 29 May 2025. Grokbot's own Date basis says 'Adopted 29 May 2025', so the date should be 2025-05-29.

withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: The workbook stores every List_date at month precision, and 2025-05-01 already reflects the May 2025 adoption; Date_basis records "Adopted 29 May 2025". There is no error.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. The workbook stores list dates to the month, so the value is right; only the date-basis label could be better. Not a Grokbot error.
